President Halsell had already begun to teach in the section, and with him they were ready to support the cause of education. All three were members of the Christian Church. This homogeneity of ideals and attitudes was an important element in the success of Savoy College.

JAMES L. GERMAN

Next to the youngest of six boys and one girl, James L. German was born in Mercer County, Missouri, May 8, 1833. His mother died when he was a child; his father, Abel German, died in 1848. In 1851 James moved with his family to Platte County, Missouri, where he was a child of Welsh descent; his mother was descended from the Tarlton family of Welsh blood. He was imbued with the high ideals and culture of aristocracy. Mr. German stood on his own feet, as the saying is. The statement was made by those who knew him, that "a man stands on its own bottom."
